function: Joint design of BS beamforming weights and RIS phase shifts (hybrid beamforming) maximizing the weighted system sum rate under power and minimum-rate constraints (p. 5-6).
system: Multi-antenna BSs (Mb=4 to 32), passive reflecting RIS (Nr=4 to 32 elements), K=4 to 32 users; OFDM transmission, frequency band not stated (p. 4-5, p. 10).
method: HBRIC-DDPG: actor-critic DDPG with CNN and fully connected layers, prioritized experience replay; reinforcement learning; continuous actions are BS weights and RIS phases (p. 6-9).
data_channel: Own simulation: steering-vector LoS plus CN(0,1) NLoS with Rician factor, fixed BS and RIS positions, random user positions, distances scaled down; no public dataset (p. 10).
test_conditions: Learning curves and sum rates per configuration; sweeps of transmit power, RIS size, users, Rician factor, learning rate, decay; no unseen-condition test of a trained model (p. 10-12).
baselines: Non-learned: WMMSE, one curve at one configuration (Mb=4, Nr=10, K=4). Learned: none compared (p. 10-11).
metrics: System sum rate (bps/Hz) versus transmit power; average reward (sum rate minus QoS penalty) versus training steps under varied settings (p. 10-12).
complexity: Order of complexity: per-update O(I0 Il + sum Il Il+1) (Eq. 32), whole training over actor, critic, sampling (Eq. 33); no runtime or FLOPs (p. 9-10).
openness: none; no code or data link (p. 1-13).
q1_support: p. 10: "by random modeling and follow the following distribution" (CN(0,1) NLoS) and "Krician denotes the corresponding channel fading coefficient"; custom Rician simulator, no 3GPP, DeepMIMO, or measured channel.
q2_support: p. 11: "convergence and effectiveness are compared under varying" Rician factors in Fig. 6, as separate learning curves; p. 5: "is completed, it can be directly deployed and used", but no trained model is tested on an unseen scenario.
q3_support: p. 10: "and analyzed with the traditional optimization scheme"; "minimum mean-square error (WMMSE) is evaluated with the" same configuration is the only comparison scheme and is non-learned; no earlier learned method is compared.
q4_support: p. 9: "of the entire HBRIC-DDPG can be approximated as" an order expression (Eq. 33), after the per-update order of Eq. 32; no runtime or FLOPs.
q5_support: p. 10: "by random modeling and follow the following distribution": own simulated channels; no code or data link and no public dataset in the paper.
notes: Included, area 3: DDPG learns BS beamforming weights and RIS phase shifts to maximize the sum rate; the 'large model' label is a claim, the networks are a CNN plus fully connected actor and critic. q3 is 0 because the only baseline is WMMSE (one curve in Fig. 4, p. 10) and no learned baseline is compared. q2 is 0 despite the 'generalized scenes' title: each configuration is a separate learning curve and no trained model is applied to an unseen one. Table I (p. 10) lists 8 BS antennas and 16 RIS elements while figures use Mb=4 or other sizes.
